nodes.body: `toolsById` is built via `Object.fromEntries(tools.map(...))`, which typically widens the key type to `string` (and can lose the `ToolId` union) under TypeScript, reducing type-safety for lookups. Consider defining `type Tool = (typeof tools)[number]` / `type ToolId = Tool['id']` before this and annotating `toolsById` as `Record<ToolId, Tool>` (or using `satisfies`) so the mapping stays aligned with the `selectedTool: ToolId` type.

To maintain an auditable and reproducible decision log, please store benchmark results or evidence in the project's established evidence directory (e.g., `docs/evidence/`) or provide a summary of the benchmark methodology and results directly in the decision log.

The use of `Object.fromEntries` without explicit typing results in `toolsById` being inferred as an object with `any` values in many TypeScript configurations. This bypasses the strict type safety previously provided by `tools.find()`. Since this project enforces a "no any" policy (as noted in `DECISIONS.md` line 910), please add a type cast to ensure the lookup remains type-safe.

```
const toolsById = Object.fromEntries(tools.map((t) => [t.id, t])) as Record<
		(typeof tools)[number]['id'],
		(typeof tools)[number]
	>;
	type ToolId = (typeof tools)[number]['id'];
```
